title: Your First Weekend at Bryn Mawr College, Shared as Cards
description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Arrive Through the Arch
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Move-In
cards.notes: Pass through the iconic Pembroke Arch to check in. This central gateway serves as the primary landmark for new students arriving on campus for Customs week.
cards.short_summary: The historic stone gateway where new students officially enter campus life during move-in.
cards.evidence_claim: New students arrive and check in during the morning of move-in day, often passing through Pembroke Arch as a central campus landmark.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a pedestrian thoroughfare; vehicle access is restricted during move-in events.

cards.title: First Group Brunch
cards.subtitle: Saturday at 11:00 AM
cards.notes: Gather with your new hallmates for brunch in this Brutalist landmark. It is the primary weekend dining hub for the first-year community.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive Brutalist dining hall serving as the main social hub for weekend meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Erdman Dining Hall serves brunch from 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM on Saturdays and Sundays during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: Erdman Dining Hall - Bryn Mawr College
cards.access_notes: Requires a student meal plan or OneCard for entry during meal hours.

cards.title: Lawn Games and Lounging
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon
cards.notes: Relax on the sloping lawn behind Rhoads Hall. Students frequently use this green space for frisbee, reading, and meeting new friends outdoors.
cards.short_summary: A popular grassy slope on campus used for outdoor recreation and social gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhoads Beach is a rolling, grassy area located behind Rhoads Hall used by students for outdoor activities.

cards.title: Explore the Bi-Co
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening
cards.notes: Take the shuttle to Haverford College to see the other half of the Bi-College community. It is a quick 10-minute ride from Pembroke Arch.
cards.short_summary: The inter-campus shuttle connecting Bryn Mawr and Haverford students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Bus provides transportation between Bryn Mawr and Haverford, with departures from Pembroke Arch on a regular weekend schedule.
cards.access_notes: Free for students with a valid Bi-Co or Tri-Co ID card.

cards.title: Late Night Study Break
cards.subtitle: Saturday at 9:00 PM
cards.notes: Visit this student-run cafe in the basement of Canaday Library for a late-night snack. It is a favorite spot for social study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A student-run cafe located in Canaday Library known for its late-night hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lusty Cup is a late-night cafe on the lower floor of Canaday Library, typically open from 8:00 PM to 12:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Open late night during the academic year; check library hours for specific weekend access.

cards.title: Reflect in the Cloisters
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning
cards.notes: Walk through the serene courtyard of the Old Library. This space is central to many college traditions and offers a quiet place for reflection.
cards.short_summary: A historic, Gothic-style courtyard within the Old Library building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cloisters in the Old Library is an active student space used for quiet reflection and major traditions like Lantern Night.
cards.source_title: History of Old Library - Bryn Mawr College
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students during building hours; often used for quiet study.

cards.title: Prep for First Classes
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon
cards.notes: Find a carrel or a table in Canaday to organize your syllabus and books. The library is the primary academic resource center on campus.
cards.short_summary: The main library on campus providing extensive study spaces and research resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Canaday Library is the main library at Bryn Mawr, offering various study spaces including Quita's Corner and computer labs.
cards.access_notes: Open to students with OneCard access; weekend hours typically start at 12:00 PM.

cards.title: Community Gathering
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening
cards.notes: Join fellow students on the large central lawn for informal gatherings. It is the heart of campus and the site of many major outdoor events.
cards.short_summary: The central green space of the campus, used for major events and daily student life.
cards.evidence_claim: Merion Green is the central lawn of the college, hosting events like May Day and serving as a general student gathering spot.

cards.title: Afternoon Tea Tradition
cards.subtitle: Sunday at 4:00 PM
cards.notes: Experience the long-standing tradition of afternoon tea. It is a formal yet welcoming way to connect with the college's history and community.
cards.short_summary: A historic house on campus that hosts traditional afternoon tea services.
cards.evidence_claim: Wyndham Alumnae House offers afternoon tea, a tradition that has been part of the college experience for decades.
cards.access_notes: Tea service is available to the college community; check for specific student seating times.

cards.title: Safe Evening Transit
cards.subtitle: Sunday Night
cards.notes: Use the student-driven shuttle for a safe ride back to your dorm after a long weekend of exploring. It connects campus and local train stations.
cards.short_summary: A student-run evening transportation service for the Bryn Mawr community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lantern Shuttle runs nightly from 7:00 PM to 1:00 AM, providing safe transport for students around campus and to local transit.
cards.access_notes: Available to all students with a valid Bryn Mawr ID; runs 7 PM - 1 AM daily.
